summary: FAIL. The original multi-version reuse goal has NOT been durably achieved at the cited checkpoint HEAD 143642b. Independent audit at HEAD 143642bfea6752b573c7b9cb56bfcf0c191b0d95 confirms: (1) The ENTIRE M6 migration wiring — 32 m6_authority_route tool registrations in server.py, the m6_authority_route function in authority.py, index_legacy_db_into_m6 wired into runner.py, and the untracked m6_production_indexing.py — exists ONLY as uncommitted working-tree state. git show HEAD:<each file> returns ZERO m6_* matches; git log -S 'm6_authority_route' is empty; m6_production_indexing.py is untracked; 119 files are dirty. (2) The M7 program's OWN frozen authority matrix (authority_matrix.json, frozen at HEAD 143642b, code-derived by M7_BOOTSTRAP_LEAD) declares that at HEAD 143642b: production read authority = v2, production write authority = v2, m6_status = SHADOW_ONLY, m6_involvement_in_read_path = NONE, m6_involvement_in_write_path = NONE. The IMMUTABLE_M7_MASTER_GOAL.md §5 and M7_AUTHORITY_DEFINITIONS.md confirm this is the frozen STARTING POINT of M7. (3) The M7.1-M7.5 gate result files + all evidence files claim 'verified at HEAD 143642b' with M6 as production authority (32 m6-native reads, v2 retired) — the exact OPPOSITE of the contract's frozen baseline at the same HEAD. The gates ran against the dirty working tree and misattributed the results to the committed HEAD. (4) Per §2 authority priority (contracts > hard gates > runtime > evidence > narration), the contract (priority 1) declaring HEAD 143642b = v2 authority OUTRANKS the gate evidence (priority 2/5) claiming HEAD 143642b = M6 authority; the program's PASS declarations violate this. (5) §17 dirty-state identity and §19 M7-owned diff-hash disclosure were NEVER recorded (grep across .dsh-control/m7/** = no matches), so the §19 escape-hatch for uncommitted state was not honored; the evidence presents working-tree results as committed-HEAD results. (6) Economic Closure is 6/8 PASS with E7 (this verifier) and E8 (guardian) PENDING. IMPORTANT NUANCE: the migration is BEHAVIORALLY genuine, not a §8 anti-false-migration fake — the working-tree m6_authority_route really does route to M6 query adapters that read the real M6 store (no silent fallback to v2; RuntimeError on missing store), M6 production indexing is really wired into runner.py (raises IndexIntegrityError on failure), v2 finalize is really gated off, and normal_path_dependencies_state.json really shows all 4 v2 counts = 0. The failure is one of PROVENANCE, DURABILITY, and AUTHORITY-PRIORITY: the achievement is uncommitted, attributed to a HEAD whose frozen contract baseline declares the opposite authority, with no diff-hash disclosure. To close the goal: commit the M7-owned M6 wiring to a durable checkpoint, re-derive the frozen authority matrix + contract baseline against that new HEAD so contract and gates agree, re-run all M7 hard gates + scanners against the committed checkpoint, record dirty-state identity / diff hash per §17/§19, then run fresh Verifier + fresh Guardian against that exact committed HEAD. As it stands, at the cited HEAD 143642b, v2 remains the production read+write authority and M6 remains shadow-only — the original multi-version reuse goal is NOT closed.
